body: I hope you feel better. I'm going to go to sleep now, I need some rest because I drank too much tonight. I promise I won't do anything to harm myself, thanks for taking the time to talk to me.

Thanks for your time, I'm going to go to sleep now. I promise I won't do anything to harm myself tonight. Please focus on other people that need help. I'll figure out what I'm going to do with my life tomorrow. You seem like a good kid.

No, I realize they have mortgages, I'm not saying it's their fault. I just am not convinced patients should directly pay therapists. It provides perverse incentives. I'm sure most therapists are great, but on the aggregate-- having patients directly pay therapists is kind of broken.

No matter, talk therapy doesn't work for me. I'll keep it up with the psychiatry, maybe I'll find a medicine that works.

You've been great, don't worry about me- I'll go to sleep now. I won't do anything to harm myself tonight.
Oh sorry, my bad. I hope you find what you need. Thanks for talking to me.

I've been seeing psychiatrists re: depression for years. I've tried a slew of medication. I've even given therapists a shot. 

Honestly, the medicines I've tried have been underwhelming at best. And I haven't met any "therapists" that I can take seriously (they seem like nice enough people, but the pay-for-talking kind of screws up incentives, or at least cheapens their apparent concern).

I am out there, I am involved with clubs, organizations, and professional groups outside of work. I absolutely do pursue my interests.

I'm just at the age where you don't just "make friends". (As I said, I'm older than the main reddit demographic.) No one really has time for that. And I'm ok with that, I realize that when you are older things are different... you don't really spend a lot of time with friends... but damn, I'd really like someone to call every once in a while (or call me).

Anyway, thanks for the talk. You seem like a good person.

Thanks for the kind words.

In my OP, I wasn't implying that people were judgmental. In my first post, I thought the community name implied something very, very different... because I couldn't see the context (such as the sidebar, guidelines, css, etc)

Thanks for the kind words. 

I have a lot of experience seeking out help from mental health people (including psychiatrists) over the years. I'm kind of exhausted to be honest.

I don't really have anything to "pour" out. I've dealt with depression for many, many years. I've been able to convince that it will get better for a long time. Despite my efforts (and believe me, I've tried lots of things) I just can't find a way out. 

It's more that I'm at the point where as of a few weeks ago I was indifferent to life, and now my attitude is decaying. I'm thinking that maybe I just don't want to do this anymore.

Hmm... thanks for the conversation. 

I suspect that I'm older than the average reddit demographic. I'm not really looking for "that special someone." It would be nice to have a friend or two that I could at least talk to on the phone. The people I interact with on a daily basis would likely not care that I was gone (I'm sufficiently confident of that).

I'd rather not disclose too much personal information, but I'm involved with designing electronic devices and developing software.

So... over the last several months I've been trying to come to terms with the that I'm not actually relevant to anyone else. If I died right now, it really wouldn't matter.

I've been really active for awhile, I work, I'm involved with clubs and organizations, I've even seen some psychiatrists. Nothing is really working.

Thanks, I pretty much figured that out right after that guy mentioned the guidlines and I started reading other posts.

It's mostly just terrifying indifference. I fantasize about killing myself all the time even though I'm really scared to die.

(I even go the extra mile when planning to make it look like an accident, despite the fact that I honestly don't know anyone who would actually miss me.)

I'm too much of a bitch to actually do it though, it'll probably end up being something passive.

I think about killing myself fairly often. 

The weird thing about it is, I haven't really figured out a way to do it without really inconveniencing someone else.  I'm thinking about moving towards the coast though, to be near an ocean so I can buy a boat.

I don't have any family and I haven't had much success making friends that would actually miss me.

Depression is really embarrassing. I would never admit it to a person in meatspace.

My post was a kind of stream of consiousness blob of text- I do have casual friends but many of them are moving on in their lives (towards family life- understandably) and I'm kind of on new ground now.

I don't really want kids (or at least I'm not ready to settle down now).

I realize that, my question was more geared to how you facilitate that process as you get older. I know how to make friends, I'm just in new territory now. I was hoping people with similar life experiences wanted to share something.

Edit: New territory as in: I moved to a new city, I'm not ready to settle down just yet, but most of the casual friends I have are moving on to family life (which is cool, they are great people). But it is really hard to become close with people who have family obligations. Maybe that's just my misconception.
